      Run the application as administrator to move shares. Every step needs administrator rights on this server and on the old server.

      1. Connect to the old server

      Type the name of the server the shares are on now. This server is the new one.

      Connect as
      An administrator on the old server. Used only to reach the old server, for every step. The password is kept in memory until you close the application or start over, and is never saved.

        2. Choose shares

        Tick the shares to move and choose where each one goes on this server. Then check the plan: it measures each share and checks free space and permissions. Nothing is copied yet.

        Puts each selected share in its own folder inside the folder you choose. Or use Browse on a share. New folders are created when copying starts.

        3. Copy

        Users can keep working on the old server while you copy. Each copy after the first brings over only what changed, so copy again as often as you like.

        Copies files, folders, timestamps and NTFS permissions with Robocopy. Files removed from the old share are also removed from the copy.

        4. Cut over

        Ask users to stop using the old shares first. Cutover makes a final copy, creates the shares on this server with the old share settings and permissions, and compares the old and new files.

        After cutover (optional)

        Make the old shares read-only

        Stops anyone saving new files on the old server by mistake. The old permissions are saved so you can undo this.

        Find DFS links to update

        Lists DFS namespace links that still point at the old server, with the new path to use.

        Give this server the old server's name

        Lets old paths that use the old server's name keep working. Only after the old server is shut down.
        Then update mapped drives, logon scripts, Group Policy drive maps and shortcuts that use the old server's name, unless you gave this server that name.

          Migration scenario

          How the move uses hardware. The rest of Migration and replication follows this choice: the new cluster's size, Build Hyper-V hosts, the waves, Migration plans and the runbook.

          New cluster size

          Describe the new cluster to check that the VMs you are moving fit, with room for a node to fail.

          Stages: one host at a time

          Each stage empties one host onto the hosts still running the old platform, takes it out, rebuilds it as a node of the new cluster and moves a wave of VMs onto the nodes rebuilt so far. Both sides are checked at every stage, with a host kept free for a failure (N+1) where there are enough. Everything here can be changed: the order, the host each stage rebuilds, the wave it moves, whether the wave moves before the host is emptied, and stages that only move VMs. Change which VMs are in each wave in Waves below.

            Networks and storage

            Name the network and VLAN each VMware network becomes, and where each datastore's disks go. The runbook uses these names.

            Waves

            What is a wave? A group of VMs you move together in one maintenance window, for example wave 1 on Friday night and wave 2 the week after. Small waves keep each cutover short and let you test before moving the next group.

            Suggest waves is a starting point: powered-off, test and development VMs first, one domain controller early and the others last (never two together), each database server alone, servers of one application together, and VMware system and backup appliances left out. Each VM says why it was put where it is. Then change anything: drag VMs between waves, rename a wave, give it a planned date, move waves up or down, split or merge them. VMs you place by hand are kept when you suggest again.

                Every copy, whether from Move VMs, Replicate servers or Send here, goes to a receiver on the new machine. On a Hyper-V host or any Windows computer, start Receive here: each disk is saved as a VHDX file. A new HyperCore, Nutanix, Proxmox or physical machine boots receiver media instead and writes each disk straight onto its own disks. Send copies the disks of the computer it runs on by hand, for one machine without the replication agent; sending again later sends only what changed. To keep servers in sync until a scheduled cutover, use Replicate servers; to move a VMware or Hyper-V VM with nothing installed in it, use Move VMs.

                  Receiver media: for a new HyperCore, Nutanix AHV, Proxmox VE or physical machine

                  Builds a Windows PE ISO with this program as the receiver, using the Windows ADK and its Windows PE add-on on this computer. Boot the new machine from it: the receiver takes every blank disk and shows its address, thumbprint and pairing code on the console. Add the drivers the new machine needs to see its disks and network, such as the VirtIO drivers (virtio-win) for HyperCore, Nutanix and Proxmox, or the server vendor's storage and network drivers.

                  Runs on this computer. To have the VM created and started for you, use Move VMs instead.

                  Start a VM from the copies

                  A test failover starts a VM on new differencing disks whose parents are the copies, so nothing the test VM writes reaches the copies. Replication pauses for those copies while the test runs (the source keeps running) and catches up by itself when you end the test. Leave the network not connected, or choose an isolated switch, so the test VM never meets the real server on the network. Use production after the job's cutover: the VM runs from the copies themselves and they stay held.

                  VMs started from copies

                          Build Hyper-V hosts and clusters
                          Set up new Hyper-V hosts, or a failover cluster, the way the VMware environment is set up today: roles, virtual switches with the same VLANs, iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage, Cluster Shared Volumes sized from the datastores, the quorum witness and live migration. Every step first shows exactly what it will change on each computer and changes nothing until you approve it. A step can be run again at any time; it only adds what is missing and never removes anything.
                          Runs on this computer, your admin computer. It reaches each new node over PowerShell remoting (WinRM, the channel Windows Admin Center and Server Manager use); nothing is installed on the nodes. The cluster steps run here with your own Windows account.
                          6. Build, one step at a timePreview, check, approve
                          Run the steps in order. Preview lists what a step would change on each computer; Approve and apply makes exactly those changes and nothing else. Preview again afterwards: a finished step lists nothing to change.
                            Messages
                            Migration plans
                            Move a group of VMware or Hyper-V VMs to this Hyper-V host together. A plan copies every VM while it runs, keeps the copies in sync on a schedule, lets you test any VM on an isolated copy, and cuts VMs over now or at a time you choose. Nothing is installed in the VMs.
                            When to use this.
                            • Migration plans: many VMs from one vCenter, ESXi or Hyper-V host to this Hyper-V host or its cluster, kept in sync for days and cut over in waves.
                            • Move VMs: one VM by hand, or a remote Hyper-V host, HyperCore, Nutanix, Proxmox or a physical server.
                            • Replicate servers: physical servers, Linux, or VMs on any other hypervisor (an agent on each server).
                            Plans run while this application is open on this Hyper-V host, signed in to vCenter or ESXi in Discovery. Leave it open for scheduled copies and cutovers.

                            New migration plan

                            Choose the VMs from the inventory read in Discovery. Waves come from Plan and runbook; the network map there names the Hyper-V switch for each network.

                            The new VMs

                            VMWaveStateLast syncNextCutover
                            No VMs selected.

                            Cut over the selected VMs

                            Each VM's guest is shut down through VMware Tools (or the Hyper-V shutdown service), its last changes are copied and verified, and the Hyper-V VM is created on the copies. VMs cut over in wave order, each on its own: one failing never stops the others, and a VM whose final copy fails is never created. Test first: a test VM runs on differencing disks with its network disconnected, so production is untouched, and syncs for that VM wait until you end the test.

                            All jobs and servers
                            Everything this console moves, replicates, converts or restores, in one list: agent replication jobs, Migration plans, Move VMs copies, disk conversions, restores and file share moves, servers with the agent but no job, and the VMs of the inventory read in Discovery that nothing moves yet. Tick as many as you like and act on them together; Open takes you to the tool with that job's own settings.
                            How it works. Each row shows how it is moved and one state from the same set for every method. Initial copy means the first full copy is running; In sync means a whole copy exists and stays current, so it can be tested and cut over. Actions run one server after another through each method's own rules, and one server failing never stops the others. Migration plans and test failovers from replication copies show only when this runs on the Hyper-V host that holds them.
                            No servers selected.

                            Install the agent on the selected servers

                            Runs on this computer and installs the replication agent on each server: Windows through its administrative share (a signed service, no PowerShell on the server), Linux over SSH. Edit the list if a VM's name in the guest differs. Linux servers whose SSH key is new are shown in Replicate servers to check and trust.

                            Create replication jobs for the selected servers

                            Each server gets one job named after it that copies every disk, system disk first, as SERVER-disk0.vhdx, SERVER-disk1.vhdx and so on, so the new VM boots from its first disk. The copies are written by a receiver, a small listener on the Hyper-V host that saves them in one folder. When this console runs on that host, choose This computer and the receiver is started and paired for you. Receiver media for one new HyperCore, Nutanix, Proxmox or physical machine takes one server: set those jobs up in Replicate servers.

                            Put the selected servers in a wave

                            Cut over in waves uses these numbers: wave 1 first, then wave 2 after the gap you choose. VMs in a Migration plan keep the wave in their plan; agent replication jobs keep it on this console. 0 takes them out of any wave.

                            Cut over the selected servers

                            Agent replication: the services you listed stop, a final round copies the last changes and the server shuts down if the job says so; a failure restarts the services and replication carries on. Migration plans: the guest shuts down through VMware Tools or the Hyper-V shutdown service, a final verified copy runs and the Hyper-V VM is created; a VM whose final copy fails is never created. Test first.

                                Replicate whole servers
                                Install the replication agent on the servers you are moving, physical or virtual, then keep every disk copied to the new machine until you cut over. Each round sends only what changed, so the copy stays a few minutes behind. Jobs keep running on the servers when this window is closed.
                                
        
                                
          
                                
          
                                
          
                                
            
                                
              
                                Install the agent on the servers you are copying
                                
              
                                Only the source servers get the agent. The new machines run a receiver instead: Receive on a Hyper-V host or other Windows computer, or receiver media on a new HyperCore, Nutanix, Proxmox or physical machine. 
                                
              
              
                                Runs on this computer and installs the agent as a Windows service on each server through its administrative share. You need administrator rights there and File and Printer Sharing allowed. To install it by hand instead, run SIMM-Agent.exe --agent-install as administrator on the server and add it below.
                                
              
                                Runs on this computer and installs the agent as a systemd service on each server over SSH, using simm-agent-linux-amd64 from the folder this program is in (download it from the same release). Use root or an account that may use sudo. The first time, the server's SSH key is shown so you can check and trust it. Logical volumes on LVM are copied from LVM snapshots; other mounted partitions are copied as they are. To install by hand, run sudo ./simm-agent-linux-amd64 --agent-install on the server and add it below.

                                  Alerts
                                  
              
                                  A job raises an alert when its recovery point is older than its RPO limit, when three rounds fail in a row, or when a cutover is rolled back. Agents also write them to the server's Application event log (source SIMM Replication Agent, events 1001 to 1003) for your monitoring tools.

                                    Test failover on the target platform
                                    
              
                                    For copies received by receiver media in a VM on Scale Computing HyperCore, Nutanix AHV or Proxmox VE. Runs from this computer: the job pauses when its current round ends, the platform clones the receiver VM (the clone gets its own disks) and replication resumes at once. The clone's network is disconnected, it is set to start from its disk and started. Ending the test turns the clone off and deletes it; the receiver VM and its disks are never changed.
                                    
              
                                    
              
                                    
                
                                    
                
                                    
                
                
                                    
              
                                    
              
                                    
              
              
                                    
              
                                      
              
                                      
              
                                      
            
                                      
            
                                      Cut over
                                      
            
                                      Cutover stops the listed services, takes the last snapshots, sends the last changes and checks every disk against its hashes. If any step fails, the services start again and replication carries on. Start the new machine once the job says Cut over.
